summary: This government bill would create the Maldives Intellectual Property Office, a government office under the ministry responsible for economic policy, to register and protect intellectual property such as trademarks, copyright, patents, industrial designs and geographical indications. The office would be led by a Registrar of Intellectual Property, appointed and removed by the Minister, who would keep a public register of all registered intellectual property. The bill sets qualifications, a 5-year term, conduct and confidentiality rules for the Registrar and staff. It also creates a way to ask for a Registrar's decision to be reviewed, then to go to court, and a complaints system for the office's services. It is a new law, not an amendment, and has 34 articles in five chapters.
whyItMatters: Businesses, creators and inventors would register and check intellectual property through one dedicated office with a public register and set deadlines to challenge its decisions. The attached cost estimate puts running costs at about MVR 1.3 million a year.
keyProvisions: Article 4 creates the Maldives Intellectual Property Office under the ministry, with the Minister answerable to Parliament for it; Article 5 lists its duties, including registering intellectual property, keeping the register, public awareness programmes, international cooperation and collecting fees set in the intellectual property laws.

Articles 7 to 12 say the Minister appoints the Registrar within 30 days of the law taking effect, for a 5-year term that can be renewed once; the Registrar must be a Maldivian with a first degree in intellectual property, law or a related field and at least 10 years of management experience, and cannot hold a political party post or sit on a company board.

Articles 15 to 20 require the Registrar and staff to work free of political or other influence, step away from cases where they have a personal interest, refuse gifts and keep information confidential, including trade secrets, except for lawful investigations or court orders; they are protected from lawsuits for acts done in good faith.

Articles 21 to 24 require the Registrar to keep a register of intellectual property recording the owner, rights, registration date, protection period, transfers and licences, and to make it available to the public, including digitally.

Articles 26 to 29 let a person who disagrees with a Registrar's decision ask for a review within 14 days; the Registrar must decide within 45 days after advice from a review committee, and the person can go to court within 30 days.

Article 30 requires a complaints system for the office's services, Article 32 gives the Registrar 6 months to publish regulations, and Article 33 says the law takes effect 3 months after it is published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Businesses, creators and inventors who register or use trademarks, copyright, patents and designs in the Maldives, and the staff of the new office.
statedReasons: The note says the government wants a strong system to protect and develop intellectual property, encourage creativity and investment in business and support economic growth, by setting up this office and setting its duties, powers and enforcement rules.
